about: The share of each kind of seller's household sales that the sales tax does not reach, by its classification: medical care, tuition, insurance, rent and most services are outside the base in most states, and Hawaii, New Mexico and South Dakota tax most services. Read by syncSalesTax (src/core2/modules/budgets.ts) as exemptions of the tax itself, no law's. Sellers not listed (stores, restaurants, lodging) are taxed on all they sell, but for the grocery exemption where it is law. A state's own share replaces the national one where `states` names it. Every value is ESTIMATED from memory; the container could not reach the Federation of Tax Administrators' services survey to quote it.

exemptShare.citation: Medical care is exempt from the sales tax in every state that has one (FTA services survey), from memory.
Hospital care is exempt from the sales tax in every state that has one but Hawaii (FTA services survey), from memory.
Nursing and residential care is exempt in every sales-tax state but Hawaii, whose excise reaches it (FTA services survey), from memory.
Tuition is exempt in every sales-tax state (FTA services survey), from memory.
Insurance premiums bear a premium tax, never the sales tax, in every state (NAIC), from memory.
Bank fees are outside the sales tax base in every state (FTA services survey), from memory.
Agents' commissions and property managers' fees are untaxed but for Hawaii and New Mexico (FTA services survey), from memory.

Legal, accounting, design and other professional services are untaxed in nearly every state; Hawaii's general excise tax, New Mexico's gross receipts tax and South Dakota's sales tax reach most services sold to households (FTA, 2017 survey of services taxation; Hawaii Rev. Stat. 237, N.M. Stat. 7-9, S.D. Codified Laws 10-45), from memory, not fetched.

As professional services; Hawaii's general excise tax, New Mexico's gross receipts tax and South Dakota's sales tax reach most services sold to households (FTA, 2017 survey of services taxation; Hawaii Rev. Stat. 237, N.M. Stat. 7-9, S.D. Codified Laws 10-45), from memory, not fetched.

A builder's labor is untaxed in most states, its materials taxed when it buys them; Hawaii's general excise tax, New Mexico's gross receipts tax and South Dakota's sales tax reach most services sold to households (FTA, 2017 survey of services taxation; Hawaii Rev. Stat. 237, N.M. Stat. 7-9, S.D. Codified Laws 10-45), from memory, not fetched.
Freight and moving services are untaxed in most states (FTA services survey); Hawaii and New Mexico tax them, from memory.

Hair, nail, laundry and other personal services are taxed in about a fifth of sales-tax states, from memory; Hawaii's general excise tax, New Mexico's gross receipts tax and South Dakota's sales tax reach most services sold to households (FTA, 2017 survey of services taxation; Hawaii Rev. Stat. 237, N.M. Stat. 7-9, S.D. Codified Laws 10-45), from memory, not fetched.

Cleaning, landscaping and pest control are taxed in about a third of sales-tax states, from memory; Hawaii's general excise tax, New Mexico's gross receipts tax and South Dakota's sales tax reach most services sold to households (FTA, 2017 survey of services taxation; Hawaii Rev. Stat. 237, N.M. Stat. 7-9, S.D. Codified Laws 10-45), from memory, not fetched.

Repair labor is taxed in about half of sales-tax states, parts in all, from memory; Hawaii's general excise tax, New Mexico's gross receipts tax and South Dakota's sales tax reach most services sold to households (FTA, 2017 survey of services taxation; Hawaii Rev. Stat. 237, N.M. Stat. 7-9, S.D. Codified Laws 10-45), from memory, not fetched.

Admissions and memberships are taxed in most sales-tax states, from memory; Hawaii's general excise tax, New Mexico's gross receipts tax and South Dakota's sales tax reach most services sold to households (FTA, 2017 survey of services taxation; Hawaii Rev. Stat. 237, N.M. Stat. 7-9, S.D. Codified Laws 10-45), from memory, not fetched.
Phone and cable service is taxed by the sales tax or a utility tax in most states; internet access is untaxed by federal law (Internet Tax Freedom Act), from memory.
Household electricity and gas are exempt from the state sales tax in about half of sales-tax states, from memory; water and sewer charges mostly untaxed.
A farm's sales to households are food or sales for resale, untaxed in most states, from memory.
Sales for resale or for use in making goods are exempt everywhere; households buy little from a plant, from memory.
Sales for resale are exempt everywhere, from memory.
Sales for resale or further processing are exempt everywhere, from memory.
A head office bills its own firms, never households; such charges are outside the base everywhere, from memory.
